deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a fair-copy prose passage in German Kurrent script about ancient Greek history, specifically the Theban hegemony. It continues the previous page's account of Pelopidas, Epaminondas and Alexander of Pherae.

Content of the page:
(1) The end of the sentence about Pelopidas at the battle of Cynoscephalae (364 BC). He made a personal attack on Alexander of Pherae and fell. A marginal note marked '+' (roughly 'den Barbaren/Tyrannen') is keyed to this line.
(2) The Arcadians were divided, some on the Theban side and some on the Spartan side. So Thebes sent a new army into the Peloponnese under Epaminondas. A marginal date reads '362 vor Chr.'
(3) The Spartans sent an army against him, and the two met near Mantinea.
(4) Epaminondas tried to outflank the Spartan army with a night march on Sparta. By chance the Spartans learned of it too early, took a shorter route, and arrived at Sparta at the same time.
(5) A furious fight began before the walls of the city. This continues on the next page with the battle of Mantinea and Epaminondas's death.

The text reads like lecture notes or a school exercise in history, and the page number 107 is in a later hand. It may not be in Gauss's own hand. There are no formulas, numbers (other than dates) or derivations to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors. Historical remark: the next page dates the battle of Mantinea to '27 Juni 363', while this page's margin gives 362 BC. The standard date is 362 BC, so the page margin is correct and the next page's date is inconsistent.
